speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and have difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To begin our assessment, can you tell me exactly when this pain occurs and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain when eating sounds like the auriculotemporal nerve may be irritating the graft; is this aching more prominent on your right side, and does pressing on the area in front of your ear elicit pain? Also, have you noticed any new sounds like clicking, crackling, or a feeling of fullness in that ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Post-Tympanoplasty).

The pain triggered by chewing is characteristic of this condition caused by the auriculotemporal nerve; please refrain from wearing earrings on the right side to avoid pressure on the graft while we monitor for resolution.
